page: Amazon Web Services r8gd.12xlarge is an ARM-based, memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton4 architecture. It provides 48 physical cores across 48 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core, operating at 2.8 GHz via the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture. The instance features 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For I/O and communication, it provides 2850 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system does not include discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded and memory throughput. The instance reaches a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 23486.0 and stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 81850.58. Large-block read memory bandwidth achieves 402.07 GB/sec, while write bandwidth reaches 201.0 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Application-specific tests demonstrate strong results, including 47307.31 in PassMark database operations, 100.54 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, and 102.33 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-core performance falls in the middle 50%, with Geekbench single-core at 1854.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1706.69.

The 1:8 memory-to-vCPU ratio paired with fast local NVMe storage makes this instance cost-effective for large memory-bound footprints that require dedicated single-threaded execution units. The Graviton Neoverse-V2 design delivers high memory and parallel compute density, but applications requiring specialized x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX must be adapted for ARM64. Consequently, the instance is best suited for in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency Clang build farms, and I/O-intensive transactional database engines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gd.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 48 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.8 GHz, 384.0 GB of RAM, and 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Lacking GPUs, it is tailored for throughput and high memory density with a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and 22 Gbps baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier memory bandwidth (402.07 GB/sec uncached reads) and strong multi-core scaling, reaching 23486.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 81850.58 in stress-ng multi-core tests. It excels in database workloads, recording 47307.31 in PassMark database operations and over 100 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread speeds are standard, its massive parallel execution and low-latency storage deliver strong efficiency for in-memory databases, distributed caches, and I/O-heavy enterprise data processing.
